opportunities.text: The drift toward illustrative code generation We are building a massive, automated library of high-level examples that no one intends to compile. The utility is purely rhetorical. The data, captured from real-world developer conversations via GitHub share links, indicates that LLM-generated code is primarily used for demonstrating high-level concepts or providing examples in documentation. opportunities.title: The coordination tax of distributed observability
opportunities.text: The coordination tax of distributed observability Distributed monitoring usually fails because of the coordination tax. We spend most of our engineering effort building consensus protocols, managing heartbeat timeouts, and synchronizing state across a fleet of individual nodes. We treat the monitor as just another service that needs to be scheduled, scaled, and kept alive. This turns the act of observing a system into a second, equally complex system that must be managed. The overhead is rarely worth the precision. The paper by Giorgio Audrito, Ferruccio Damiani, Volker Stolz, and Mirko Viroli suggests a different direction.
